source.title: Overloading Large Vision-Language Models for Jailbreaking
source.authors: Hao-Yu Zhang; Yang-Yang Guo; Mohan S. Kankanhalli

record.tranche_reason: The study uses uncertainty in the first generated token as an optimization signal for its multimodal jailbreak attack and reports its own attack results. It does not test the listed fine-tuning, per-token KL, compliant-prefill, suffix/decoding, weight-localization, or safety-deepening claims.
record.gate_note: The study measures refusal rates and first-token entropy for simple versus complex multimodal prompts, and reports harmful-response attack success rates. These findings concern multimodal prompt complexity and jailbreaking, not any of the specified claim versions. It also reports information-flow measures and attack results; citations to other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study builds a multimodal prompt-overloading jailbreak (INFER/INFER+). It cites Qi et al. (2025) to treat the first token as the refusal indicator, then uses first-token entropy as its optimization signal. It reports only its own attack's ASR, transfer, defense and probing results. There is no fine-tuning, no aligned-vs-base per-token KL, no compliant-prefill, suffix or decoding intervention, no parameter localization and no deepening training. So it uses the shallow-alignment idea as a tool without testing any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that increasing multimodal information complexity (nested image-typography-text prompts with recursive layouts) weakens LVLM refusal and yields state-of-the-art, transferable jailbreaks. Their probes show intensified cross-modal processing and lower first-token refusal certainty.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs multimodal image-text jailbreaks using nested references, typography, recursive image layouts, and entropy-guided prompt optimization. It does not use fine-tuning, aligned/base KL measurement, or the specified opening-prefill intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across model, dataset, prompt complexity, and defense. INFER+ attack prompts for closed-source models are optimized using Qwen2-VL as surrogate; defenses reduce ASR by different amounts.

fits_no_version.finding: Complex image-typography prompts lower refusal rates and raise first-token entropy in Qwen2-VL. Cross-modal refusal contribution (RCI) increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher multimodal prompt complexity lowers refusal and raises uncertainty at the first response token in LVLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: INFER/INFER+ achieve high harmful-response ASR on open and closed LVLMs, including under defenses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Information-overloading multimodal prompts jailbreak LVLMs, with success depending on model, dataset and defense.

record.problems: No error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported for the outcomes recorded here; several probe results are presented only in figures without numeric values in the text. ASR is judged using Llama Guard 3, with StrongREJECT/GPT-4o-mini reported separately but not extracted here.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 ImageTypo, CS-DJ, and TVPI ASRs; Table 2 transferability; Table 3 StrongREJECT scores; other defended methods in Table 4; and Table 5 ablations are omitted. They are comparisons, transfer/robustness results, or ablation results for the study's own attack rather than tests of the specified claim versions. Figure 6's entropy/ASR/RCI correlations are also omitted because no values are stated in the text and they do not test a listed version.

untested.parts: No aligned-vs-base per-token KL; first-token entropy is measured only on aligned models.
No compliant-prefill, adversarial-suffix or decoding-change test. The attack is complex multimodal prompting.
No weight or rank localization. Attention knockout measures cross-modal information flow, not safety-carrying parameters.
No test of data or objective causes.

record.verdict_notes: The first-token focus derives from Qi et al. (2025), cited as [39], and is used as an attack objective. Figure 6 (first-token entropy correlating with ASR and RCI) relates loosely to the first-token idea. It reports correlations without values and does not measure the V3 quantity, so it is left as fits_no_version context.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or resulting refusal/compliance rates.
No benign-data fine-tuning or resulting harmful compliance.
No compliant opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test; the study tests complex multimodal jailbreak prompts instead.
No parameter or rank localization test.
No test of whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
No training that deepens safety or test of whether such training holds up.
